shard: EC3 #20 — inline-image white-space and final/only ASCII filter

source.primary: ISO 32000-2:2020 EC3 primary PDF physical p. 283, footer printed p. 268; annotation group Issue #20 has a StrikeOut and a Caret whose /Contents is ‘its final or only filter’.
source.effective_text: §8.9.7 NOTE 2 says that after the one white-space following ID, if its final or only filter is ASCIIHexDecode or ASCII85Decode, a processor skipping the image can skip further white-space, then skip the L-count and expect EI after optional white-space.
source.other_relevant_text: §8.9.7's preceding operative sentence permits the single-white-space / ID exception when ASCIIHexDecode or ASCII85Decode is one of the filters. §7.4.1 says decoding filters in an array form a pipeline in written order and gives data Flate-compressed then ASCII85-encoded as [/ASCII85Decode /FlateDecode]. This distinguishes the final encoding stage from the first decode-array entry.

feature_review.reader_requirement: The PDF reader shall apply the corresponding decoding filter(s) to restore stream data (§7.4.1). A valid inline ASCII85-coded filter stream includes its ~> EOD bytes (§7.4.3 and stream framing rules); where an inline image has no /L, the implementation may use the first filter's framing marker to locate EI. The EC3 sentence itself is in a NOTE and describes what a processor can do to skip an image, not a SHALL requiring that optimization.
feature_review.actual_behavior: After ID, scan consumes the required single white-space character; additional whitespace stays in the encoded bytes. For filtered data without /L, data_extent calls Document::filtered_extent, which asks the first decoder in the array for its own framing. The inline dictionary expands /F and /A85 /Fl abbreviations; ordinary decoding later executes the chain in array order. The reader does not implement an image-skip-only path that discards further leading whitespace before counting bytes.
existing_assertions: crates/pdf-model/tests/inline_images.rs::a_base85_end_of_data_marker_ends_the_data — single /A85, marker beats an embedded EI token; source data is not checked through a second filter.
crates/pdf-syntax/tests/filters.rs::a_filter_array_is_a_pipeline_decoded_in_the_order_written — multi-filter decoding, but ordinary stream rather than inline-image extent.
crates/pdf-syntax/tests/filters.rs::each_stage_takes_its_own_entry_of_a_decodeparms_array — multi-stage parameters, not inline-image marker location.
feature_review.ledger: §8.9.7 is implemented and names filtered-data marker assertions; §7.4.1 is implemented with a filter-array pipeline test. No current inline-image test couples the multi-filter decode path to an outer ASCII85 EOD that must win over an EI token in the encoded text.
feature_review.adr_review: ADR 0464 supports marker-based inline-image extent; ADR 0466 rejects first-EI searching as a general strategy; ADR 0467 supports framing for filters without a resumable decoder. These premises remain applicable. The inline-image module documents that array order chooses the first filter's framing; no reviewed ADR claims multi-filter inline-image EOD is fully tested.
feature_review.verdict: No confirmed implementation defect. There is a narrow meaningful assertion gap: inline-image extent under an ASCII85 outer encoding stage has only a one-filter witness, while chain decoding is asserted separately. A valid chained fixture can cover the integration. Do not turn the NOTE's optional skip recipe into a mandatory requirement to discard additional whitespace.
residuals: The available test API returns scanned encoded bytes and decoded samples, not a skip-only operation; it cannot show whether an optional skip optimization was used.
This is not a claim that every admitted filter chain's inline-image boundary was audited.
The draft is not run in this shard.
